summary.title: Statistical mechanics of two-dimensional foams
summary.executive_summary: This paper applies the methods of statistical mechanics to two-dimensional foams under macroscopic agitation, introducing a new state variable, the total cell curvature, which plays the role of energy in conventional statistical thermodynamics. The author argues that previous theoretical approaches relying on ad-hoc interaction potentials or maximum entropy principles failed to account for the correlations between topological disorder (number of sides) and geometrical disorder (bubble size) observed in experiments. By assuming that all accessible microstates with fixed total number of sides and total cell curvature are equally probable, the paper derives a grand-canonical ensemble description. The model predicts a probability distribution for the number of sides of a cell given its area, which recovers semi-empirical expressions conjectured by other authors in a specific limit. The theoretical predictions are compared with experimental data from Quilliet et al., showing good agreement in reproducing the side number distributions and the correlation between topological and geometrical disorder. The study concludes that total cell curvature and total number of sides are the relevant variables for describing the macroscopic state of a foam, rather than surface energy, and suggests extensions to three-dimensional foams and coarsening systems.

claims.description: Total cell curvature is the appropriate state variable for 2D foams, replacing energy.
The model successfully correlates topological and geometrical disorder in 2D foams.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper applies the methods of statistical mechanics to two-dimensional foams under macroscopic agitation, introducing a new state variable, the total cell curvature, which plays the role of energy in conventional statistical thermodynamics. The author argues that previous theoretical approaches relying on ad-hoc interaction potentials or maximum entropy principles failed to account for the correlations between topological disorder (number of sides) and geometrical disorder (bubble size) observed in experiments. By assuming that all accessible microstates with fixed total number of sides and total cell curvature are equally probable, the paper derives a grand-canonical ensemble description. The model predicts a probability distribution for the number of sides of a cell given its area, which recovers semi-empirical expressions conjectured by other authors in a specific limit. The theoretical predictions are compared with experimental data from Quilliet et al., showing good agreement in reproducing the side number distributions and the correlation between topological and geometrical disorder. The study concludes that total cell curvature and total number of sides are the relevant variables for describing the macroscopic state of a foam, rather than surface energy, and suggests extensions to three-dimensional foams and coarsening systems.

Research Context
Foams and related systems serve as a paradigm for physical phenomena. Previous studies focused on topological and geometrical properties of cellular materials. Quilliet et al. studied 2D soap froths under slow oscillatory shear. Macroscopic strain induces rearrangements through local topological changes. An equilibrium state exists with a stationary probability distribution of sides. The width of the side distribution correlates with bubble size distribution. These results suggest using statistical thermodynamics ideas for sheared foams. Edwards' work on granular matter extended statistical physics to athermal systems. Previous attempts to describe 2D foams relied on strong assumptions. Some models used ad-hoc interaction potentials between bubbles. Other models involved empirical laws correlating size and side distributions. Some models ignored geometrical constraints like individual bubble areas. Maximum entropy formalism has been subject to controversy. Different arrangements of bubbles do not significantly affect energy. None of the previous models accounted for topological-geometrical correlations.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is how to describe the equilibrium state of a 2D foam. The hypothesis is that energy is not relevant for the macroscopic state. A more appropriate state variable is the total cell curvature. The model predicts a distribution of sides for a cell of given area. This expression correlates topological disorder to geometrical disorder. The model predictions should agree with available experimental data. The framework is based on analogies with conventional statistical mechanics. The thermodynamic potential differs from entropy or energy used previously. The semi-empirical expression conjectured by others is recovered in a limit. Bubble size-topology correlations are investigated and compared with experiments.

Methodological Details
The study considers a set of NB bubbles with prescribed areas. The focus is on time scales shorter than coarsening and coalescence. The foam is a partition of the plane without gaps or overlaps. The dry foam limit is considered where liquid volume is negligible. Physical constraints follow from mechanical equilibrium and Plateau's laws. Edges are three-connected making angles of 120 degrees. Edges are arcs of circles with curvature proportional to pressure difference. The algebraic curvatures of three edges meeting at a vertex sum to zero. Topological constraints include Euler's rule relating bubbles, borders, and vertices. The Gauss-Bonnet theorem is applied to n-sided cells. The microcanonical ensemble is defined by NB, total curvature, and total sides. The foam is agitated slowly compared to relaxation time after T1 events. Deformation is quasistatic, preserving the area of every bubble. All accessible microstates are hypothesized to have equal probability. The postulate applies to free clusters if surrounding air is included. Unbounded foams include infinite, periodic, or free clusters with air. Bounded foams include free finite clusters or foams in containers. Energy fluctuations are less than 2% for 2D foams under shear. Energy values of metastable states lie within 2% of ground state. Surface energy fluctuations are below 4% for 3D foams. Total number of sides Ns is a constant of motion for unbounded foams. Total cell curvature ktot is additive and zero for unbounded foams. The constraint ktot = 0 is imposed by the curvature sum rule. The microcanonical ensemble refers to copies with fixed NB, ktot, and Ns.

Procedures And Architectures
For a bounded foam, ktot reduces to the sum of boundary curvatures. Ns and ktot are fluctuating variables for bounded foams. Fluctuations of Ns and ktot become negligible in the thermodynamic limit. The average number of sides scales as NB. The total curvature scales as the square root of NB. Relative standard deviations scale as the inverse square root of NB. The idealized foam uses a mean-field approximation for the rest of the foam. Each bubble is a regular cell with identical curved sides. The cell curvature of an n-sided regular cell is given by Eq. 5. The elongation e(n) is a slowly decreasing function. The cell curvature increases rapidly with n and is not upper-bounded. The grand-canonical ensemble allows exchange of sides and curvature. The probability of a microstate is proportional to exp(-beta*ktot + mu*Ns). Beta inverse is the temperature of the curvature reservoir. Mu is the chemical potential of the sides reservoir. The probability for a cell of size A to have n sides is given by Eq. 6. The partition function chi(A) sums over all possible side numbers. The thermodynamic equilibrium corresponds to the minimum of the potential Phi. The elongation of a regular cell is almost constant at 3.72. The distribution simplifies to a Gaussian-like form in Eq. 7. Beta prime and mu prime explicitly depend on bubble size A. The average number of sides increases with area A. The theory contains no free parameters in the thermodynamic limit. Beta and mu are obtained by extremizing the grand-canonical entropy.

Key Results
For a monodisperse foam, the side number distribution tends to a Kronecker delta. All bubbles of an unbounded monodisperse foam have hexagonal shape. The theoretical distribution reproduces experimental data from Quilliet et al. well. The comparison with other distributions gives similar results. The relative standard deviation of sides is plotted against size deviation. A power-law fit agrees with the relationship found by Quillet et al. The power-law fit parameters are a = 0.30 +/- 0.03 and b = 0.74 +/- 0.08. A linear fit is also possible with a = 0.30 +/- 0.02 and b = 0.03 +/- 0.01. The power-law fit can hardly be distinguished from a linear fit. The model correlates topological and geometrical disorders.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The total number of sides and total cell curvature are relevant variables. Energy is not the relevant variable for the macroscopic state. The distribution of sides allows correlating size and shape distributions. The theoretical size-topology relations agree with existing experimental data. The formalism can be extended to three-dimensional foams. The formalism can be extended to coarsening and coalescing foams. Coarsening affects size-topology correlations as average area increases. Extension to other cellular systems like emulsions is under investigation.

Contradictions And Limitations
A free parameter was added for comparison with experiments. This is due to the indeterminacy of experimental ktot/NB values. The grand-canonical description requires 1 << NB* << NB. This condition cannot be checked on the available data. Further experiments are needed to confirm the zero-free-parameter model. The model assumes areas are fixed, ignoring coarsening effects. The mean-field approximation disconnects bubbles from each other.

Claims
Total cell curvature is the appropriate state variable for 2D foams, replacing energy. Energy fluctuations are small and do not depend on configuration. Total curvature is a conserved quantity for unbounded foams. The model recovers semi-empirical expressions using curvature. Previous models used energy minimization or maximum entropy. This shifts the statistical mechanics framework for athermal systems. It provides a parameter-free prediction for side distributions.
The model successfully correlates topological and geometrical disorder in 2D foams. Theoretical distributions match experimental data from Quilliet et al. The power-law fit of disorder correlation matches previous findings. A free parameter was needed for finite-size experimental comparison. The linear vs power-law fit ambiguity remains. Validates the use of statistical mechanics for foam equilibrium. Provides a basis for predicting foam properties from size distributions.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The model was tested against four experimental distributions. The fit was performed under the constraint that average sides is 6. The power-law and linear fits were compared for the disorder correlation. The elongation e(n) was approximated as constant for simplification.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 summarizes different boundary conditions for 2D foams. Figure 2 illustrates the equivalence between vertex and cell curvature sums. Figure 3 shows the idealization of a foam using mean-field approximation. Figure 4 compares theoretical and experimental side number distributions. Table 1 summarizes the analogy between ideal gas and 2D foam statistics.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the introduction of total cell curvature as the energy analogue. 2. The strongest evidence is the agreement with experimental side distributions. 3. The future path is extension to 3D foams and coarsening systems.
